sentence_stem: My sister works in a hospital, so
correct_completion: she helps many patients every day.
full_sentence: My sister works in a hospital, so she helps many patients every day.
acceptable_variants: she meets many doctors every day.
she looks after sick people every day.

options.text: she helps many patients every day.
she help many patients every day.
options.why_wrong: The third person singular needs the -s ending, so 'help' must become 'helps' after 'she'.

options.text: she helping many patients every day.
options.why_wrong: A main verb in the present simple does not take -ing here, and it needs a subject and a correct form.
The past tense does not match 'works' and 'every day', which describe a habit in the present.

grammar_focus: Present simple, third person singular (-s ending)
explanation: After 'so', the second clause shows the result of the first clause. The verb must take the -s ending because the subject is third person singular.
translation: Mi hermana trabaja en un hospital, así que ayuda a muchos pacientes todos los días.
